title: Quantitative 1D Borsuk-Ulam: Effective Antipodal Bound (OQ-03-OQ-04)
description: Proves effective bounds on antipodal pair location for K-Lipschitz functions: if |f(1)-f(-1)| = δ > 0, any antipodal zero x₀ of f-f(-·) lies in [-1+δ/(2K), 1-δ/(2K)]. 14 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: The Borsuk-Ulam theorem guarantees existence of an antipodal pair (f(x) = f(-x)) for any continuous f: Sⁿ → ℝⁿ. The quantitative version asks: where must the antipodal pair lie?
overview.problemStatement: For a K-Lipschitz f with |f(1)-f(-1)| = δ > 0, prove any antipodal zero x₀ satisfies x₀ ∈ [-1+δ/(2K), 1-δ/(2K)].
overview.proofStrategy: antiDiff g(x) = f(x) - f(-x) is 2K-Lipschitz and satisfies g(x₀)=0, |g(1)|=δ. Then δ = |g(1)-g(x₀)| ≤ 2K·(1-x₀) gives x₀ ≤ 1-δ/(2K). Similarly for the lower bound.
keyInsights: **Antisymmetric difference**: g(x) = f(x) - f(-x) satisfies g(-x) = -g(x), so its zeros are antipodal pairs.
**Lipschitz bound**: |g(1) - g(x₀)| ≤ 2K·|1-x₀| bounds the distance between x₀ and the boundary 1.
**Two-sided bound**: applying the same argument at -1 gives the symmetric lower bound.

conclusion.summary: 14 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms. Effective antipodal location bounds proved for K-Lipschitz functions.
conclusion.implications: Quantitative Borsuk-Ulam results are important for algorithmic applications (approximate fixed points) and for understanding how 'topologically necessary' points are distributed.
openQuestions: Can similar effective bounds be proved in higher dimensions?
Can the bound be improved for smoother functions?
Can the PPAD complexity of finding the antipodal pair be analyzed via this bound?
